gaps.sentence: 'You may leave early,' the manager said. The manager said we ___ leave early.
'I saw her yesterday,' she said. She said she had seen her ___.
gaps.explanation: Yesterday becomes the day before (or the previous day) in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: The witness ___ the police that he knew nothing.
gaps.explanation: Tell somebody that... — the personal object 'the police' requires told, not said.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll call you later,' he promised. He promised that he ___ call me later.
gaps.explanation: Will backshifts to would in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: The hijackers ___ to blow up the plane unless their demands were met.
gaps.explanation: A declared harmful action is reported as threatened to do something.

gaps.sentence: 'We stayed at this hotel last summer,' they recalled. They recalled that they had stayed at ___ hotel the summer before.
gaps.explanation: Demonstratives shift: this hotel → that hotel; last summer → the summer before.

gaps.sentence: 'I'd love to come,' she said. She said she ___ love to come.
gaps.explanation: 'I'd love' is I would love; would does not change in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'When did the ancient city fall?' we asked the guide. We asked the guide when the ancient city ___.
gaps.explanation: did...fall → had fallen: the auxiliary 'did' disappears and the verb backshifts.
